customManagers.description: Directory.Build.targets pins the implicit Microsoft.NET.ILLink.Tasks (KnownILLinkPack ILLinkPackVersion), so the lock files do not depend on the SDK patch. After a bump, regenerate every packages.lock.json (dotnet restore --force-evaluate).

Directory.Build.targets pins the implicit Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets of the Web and BlazorWebAssembly SDKs (KnownAspNetCorePack AspNetCorePackVersion), so the sample lock files do not depend on the SDK patch. After a bump, regenerate every packages.lock.json (dotnet restore --force-evaluate).

Directory.Build.targets pins the implicit Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WebAssembly.Pack of the BlazorWebAssembly SDK (KnownWebAssemblySdkPack WebAssemblySdkPackVersion), so the sample lock files do not depend on the SDK patch. After a bump, regenerate every packages.lock.json (dotnet restore --force-evaluate).

The e2e workflow installs the Playwright OS dependencies with the npm CLI of the Microsoft.Playwright pin (build/Build.CI.cs reads Directory.Packages.props), so the generated e2e.yml moves in the same PR and VerifyWorkflows stays green.

packageRules.description: SPEC §20.2: automerge minor and patch updates of dev dependencies, only through platform automerge behind the required checks. The runtime dependencies of SPEC §3 (Microsoft.Extensions.*, Microsoft.AspNetCore.*, R3) are excluded by pattern, so one a later story adds is never automerged; the test-only Microsoft.Extensions.* packages are excluded with them.

Fallout pins the actions of the generated workflows (only release.yml, pr-title.yml and docs.yml are hand-written); an edit there fails VerifyWorkflows. They move with a Fallout bump and a regeneration.

S-1 (R-PKG-3, ADR-0003): Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0 is the Roslyn of the SDK 10 line, the generator floor that consumers on SDK 10 still load, and it does not move with the SDK 11 toolchain pin of global.json (11.0.100). Never update the Roslyn pin; dotnet-sdk moves by hand, in a PR that also runs the Nuke Ci target on the new SDK. Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces (the analyzer verifier tests) stays on the same floor: it depends on exactly its own Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Common, so any other version fails the restore with NU1107 against the 5.0.0 pin.
SPEC §3: R3 stays on 1.x (1.3.x pin, packed as R3 >= 1.3.x).

test/BannedSymbols.covered.txt lists CsCheck.Check overloads by exact documentation ID, and BannedApiAnalyzers ignores an ID that no longer resolves and cannot ban an overload it is not given. Before merging, run `dotnet run test/banned-ids.cs -- check`: it fails on a listed ID that no longer resolves and on a generated overload missing from the list (a bump that adds a threads overload). Paste the cscheck group printed by `dotnet run test/banned-ids.cs` into the list, then update test/Shared/Property.cs.

These analyzers load into the repo's own compiler, and the generators must load in the Roslyn 5.0.0 of the SDK 10 line (the S-1 floor): a release built against a newer Roslyn fails an SDK 10 consumer with CS9057, which CI on SDK 11 does not see. Before merging, build a sample with the SDK 10 line (the spikes/S-1-roslyn-floor/README.md side-by-side install and a global.json with rollForward disable).
Verify 33.0.0 moved from MIT to an EULA (OSMF) whose SponsorCheck fails the build until a sponsorship or exemption is declared: the owner decides before any major bump (Directory.Packages.props).
The implicit SDK packs stay on the 11.0 line of the net11.0 target (Directory.Build.targets): they must match the SDK's own pack versions.
The 1.x legacy fixtures (docs/migration/samples/legacy) model third-party libraries as published and stay on net10.0, so their framework packages stay on 10.0.x (ADR-0049).
